data.one_liner: SIP UA stack for Flutter and Dart, supporting audio/video calls and instant messaging.
data.what_it_does: A pure Dart implementation of a SIP UA stack ported from JsSIP. It enables SIP over WebSocket and TCP, allowing Flutter mobile, desktop, and web apps to handle audio/video calls and instant messaging using standard SIP servers like Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, and OpenSIPS.
use_when: You need to build a VoIP client or softphone in Flutter with audio and video call support.
You are connecting to standard SIP servers like Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, or OpenSIPS.
You need cross-platform SIP support including iOS, Android, Web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
avoid_when: Your SIP infrastructure strictly requires UDP for the signaling process.
You only need basic push notifications for incoming VoIP calls without a full SIP stack.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms: iOS, Android, Web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Integrates with standard SIP servers (OpenSIPS, Kamailio, Asterisk, 3CX, FreeSWITCH).
Supports SIP over WebSocket and TCP as well as WebRTC-based audio/video streams.
weaknesses: Does not support UDP connection options for signaling out of the box.
Requires proper PBX configuration for DTLS/SRTP and matching codecs to avoid WebRTC setup errors.
data.setup_notes: Requires Proguard rules on Android and proper PBX server configuration for WebRTC (DTLS/SRTP and matching codecs like Opus or G.722).
